A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HALT research. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and an added evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original finetuning experiments across four models and four domains, evaluator validation, and analyses of correctness/completeness trade-offs and Add-On HALT.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a pairwise response-quality evaluation against base Llama3-70B in Section 3.2 and Table 5.

M1.justification: The few-shot generation, fragmentation, correctness filtering, percentile-based response selection, and finetuning procedures remain unchanged. Add-On HALT's uncertainty annotations already appear in v1. Clarifications and revised illustrative prompts do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Wikibios, MATH, MedExQA, and introductory APPS problems. The added AlpacaEval-style evaluation reuses these four datasets; it does not introduce the AlpacaEval dataset or document different task requirements or input conditions.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds a direct HALT-versus-base-Llama3-70B comparison for response quality. The original comparisons involving Unchanged finetuning, RandomTrim, IDK, and FactTune retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: v2 adds pairwise LLM judging of HALT at alpha = 0.6, reporting win rates excluding ties across a stated 578 prompts. Existing protocols remain stable. The new protocol is inconsistently documented: Section 3.2 names GPT-5, Table 5 names GPT-4o-mini, and the tabulated counts total 577.

E4.justification: The new Section 3.2 analysis tests whether selective abstention harms coherence and instruction following, with domain-specific comparisons in Table 5. Existing evaluator validation, few-shot versus ground-truth training comparisons, threshold analyses, and Add-On HALT analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing uncertainty displays and seed-related descriptions are unchanged. Table 5 adds counts and win rates but no confidence intervals, significance tests, repeated-run information, or other uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 5 newly reports HALT win rates of 50.8% overall, 66.0% on Wikibios, 45.4% on MATH and MedExQA, and 41.8% on introductory APPS. The original Tables 1–4 and quantitative plots retain their results; these additions are not improvements over corresponding v1 measurements.

T1.justification: The evaluator definition, fragment-dependency assumptions, percentile-selection rule, and completeness/correctness definitions remain unchanged. Added notation explanations restate existing material; neither version supplies new theorems or proofs relative to the other.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains capability-aligned partial abstention with controllable correctness/completeness and the same headline accuracy gains. The abstract drops the 4% F1-improvement statement, but the introduction retains it, so the claim is not withdrawn.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new aggregate win rate as preserving instruction following and attributes lower win rates in three domains to judges penalizing abstention. The shortened limitations discussion removes the explicit limitations concerning external information access and treating all fragments as equally valuable.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the dependent-fragment evaluator's dataset list from Wikibios to APPS. Figure 11 removes copied biography instructions from the illustrated MATH training pairs. These revise documentation without establishing experimental changes; Appendix A.2 retains the training hyperparameters, hardware, timings, and resource links.

R1.justification: v2 adds Band et al. and Stengel-Eskin et al. on verbalized uncertainty, Li et al. for AlpacaEval, and OpenAI for hallucination motivation. The prior-work contrast now includes calibrated hedging, and the introduction explicitly distinguishes capability alignment from distillation.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local edits update the title and affiliations, clarify terminology, add introductory motivation and evaluation discussion, and shorten the Add-On introduction, conclusion, and limitations. Some appendix headings are omitted or reorganized.

P2.justification: A document-wide conference-template redesign replaces the shaded title/abstract block, changes typography and margins, adds repeated headers, and substantially reflows and rescales displays. Figures 3 and 4 exchange numbering and placement, appendix figures move, and Table 5 is added. The retained quantitative plots themselves are identical.

improvement.justification: The added response-quality check, clearer prompt example, and broader related-work discussion offer benefits. However, the new evaluation has conflicting judge identities and inconsistent sample totals, while its broad no-harm interpretation lacks uncertainty analysis. Removing two substantive limitations also reduces transparency. With the core method and evidence unchanged, these competing effects do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
